text: A Hopf bifurcation, marking the onset of sustained oscillations in a dynamical system, occurs when:
choices: Two real fixed points collide and annihilate each other
A pair of complex-conjugate eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis (Re(λ) = 0)
The steady-state concentration reaches exactly zero
explanation: A Hopf bifurcation occurs precisely when a complex-conjugate eigenvalue pair crosses the imaginary axis (Re(λ) = 0, Im(λ) ≠ 0), switching a fixed point between stable and unstable spiral and giving birth to a limit cycle. Two real fixed points colliding describes a saddle-node bifurcation instead, and Jacobian symmetry or the concentration hitting zero are not the defining condition for a Hopf bifurcation.
